name: Sewell Mining Town
description: Perched at about 2,000 metres in the Andes, east of Rancagua, Sewell was built in 1905 as a company town for workers at El Teniente, the world's largest underground copper mine. The slope was too steep for vehicles, so the town climbs a great central staircase from the old railway station, lined with timber houses painted in bright greens, yellows, reds and blues. Once home to some 15,000 people, it was largely abandoned in the 1970s.
